title: Execution record
description: Version 0.1.0. The record REMARK's tool writes for every build and every execution, and the core a project's own runner can share: nothing of any one project is in it. Two kinds of record, dispatched on `kind`: a build, written once per environment built, and an execution, written once per script run in one environment, referring to its build by the image identifier when it ran in a container. A project's own fields go under an execution's `extensions`, one object per namespace, which this schema leaves open. No `format` keyword is relied on: validators skip formats they cannot check, so timestamps and remotes are patterns. A duration is meaningful only with its `where` and `conditions`, and durations are taken from a monotonic clock.

Version.description: The record schema's version, semantic; a newer schema still reads an older record. `$schema` says which document to check against.

Hash.description: A git object name, SHA-1 or SHA-256.

ImageId.description: The image ID from docker image inspect; the image's identity, since a name can move and a build is not bit-reproducible.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339 with an offset, Z allowed.

Https.description: An https address; a remote is normalized to the form the catalog names.

Recorder.description: The tool that wrote the record: REMARK's package or a project's runner.

tag.description: The tag checked out, when the catalog pins one.

dirty.description: True when `git status --porcelain` was not empty: tracked changes, or untracked files that are not ignored. A finding is not made from a dirty run.

worktree_tree.description: When dirty, the tree of the working tree as it was, written through a temporary index so that the real index is neither read nor touched: `I=$(mktemp -u); GIT_INDEX_FILE=$I git add -A && GIT_INDEX_FILE=$I git write-tree; rm -f "$I"`. The variable must reach both commands; with it on `git add` alone, write-tree reads the real index and records the commit's tree, losing the dirty state without an error. The tree identifies the exact state and can be kept as a commit.

Environment.description: The specification an environment was built or created from, as git records it in the tree that ran. Its hash identifies the specification, not the result: builds are not bit-reproducible, and repo2docker copies the whole checkout into a REMARK's image, so an image depends on the commit as well.

path.description: The directory, relative to the repository's root, with '.' for the root itself: binder for a REMARK, or wherever a project keeps an environment's files.

kind.description: How the environment is built: an image by repo2docker from binder files; an image from a Dockerfile; a conda environment on the host; a uv project on the host.

sha256.description: Over the files git records under the directory in the tree that ran: the commit's tree when the run was clean, the repository's worktree_tree when it was dirty, listed with `git ls-tree -r <tree> -- <path>`, never from the index or the files on disk, since the index can hold staged blobs and the bytes on disk can differ from the blob (line-ending conversion, clean and smudge filters, LFS). Each blob's bytes, read with `git cat-file blob <sha>`, or a symbolic link's text, is hashed alone with SHA-256; then the hash is SHA-256 of the listing of lines `<type> <mode> <sha256> <path>\n`, type `blob` or `link`, mode as git records it (100644, 100755, 120000), the path relative to the directory with '/' separators, the lines sorted bytewise on the UTF-8 path. Two specifications can then be compared file by file.

git_tree.description: The same content as git names it: `git rev-parse <tree>:<path>`, with the tree the commit's or, when dirty, the worktree_tree.

builder.description: What built it, with its version: repo2docker 2026.4.0, docker 29.1.3, conda 24.x, uv 0.9.x.

Where.description: The machine, and nothing about the run's settings, which are in `conditions`.

host.description: A name for the machine, or the continuous-integration runner's label; omitted when the operator prefers.

runtime.description: The container runtime and version, or 'none' for a build or run on the host.

Conditions.description: What the run was limited and set to.

thread_variables.description: The thread variables actually set, such as OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS, which can differ.

jit_cache.description: Whether a just-in-time compiler's cache was empty at the start, so that the duration includes compilation.

cpus.description: The CPU limit set on the run.

memory_bytes.description: The memory limit set on the run.

network.description: False when the run had no network.

duration_seconds.description: From a monotonic clock around the build or the script alone.

Termination.description: How it ended: an exit of its own; stopped at the wall cap; killed by the memory cap, which docker inspect reports as OOMKilled; or by another signal, named in `signal`. An exit code of 137 alone cannot tell the last three apart.

name.description: The image's name and tag. REMARK's tool names an image econ-ark/<name>:<the first 12 digits of the environment's sha256>, so that an unchanged specification keeps its name; the name can move to a newer build, which is why the record keeps the id.

registry.description: Where it was pushed, such as ghcr.io/econ-ark.

Build.description: One environment built or created from one specification at one commit: an image when where.runtime is a container runtime, a host environment when it is 'none'.

log.description: The build log's path, relative to the record.

Execution.description: One script run once in one environment.

run.description: The invocation this execution belongs to, when a tool runs many scripts at once, as a project's runner runs the jobs of an experiment.

manifest.description: The run's manifest, relative to the record.

script.description: reproduce.sh, reproduce_min.sh, or the entry point run, relative to the repository's root.

image.description: Required when the run was in a container (where.runtime not 'none'); its build record carries the rest.

build_record.description: The build record's path, relative to this record.

signal.description: The signal's name when termination is 'signal'.

output_dir.description: What outputs' paths are relative to: the job's output folder, or the checkout for a REMARK's reproduce.sh; itself relative to the record.

log.description: The log's path, relative to the record.

extensions.description: A project's own fields, one object per namespace; the core never reads them.
